_meta.purpose: Public UK price benchmarks the Decarbonarma agent reasons over when sanity-checking a user's quote. Ranges are 'ballpark', not valuations. NEVER present as a guarantee that a quote is good/bad — frame as 'typical range' + 'what to question'.
_meta.vat_note: All figures are with 0% VAT on domestic solar/battery/heat-pump installs, in force until 31 March 2027. After that VAT reverts to 20% — add ~20% to hardware+install. EV chargers are standard-rated.
_meta.note: Facebook 'Solar & battery UK' public quote sheets (12/16/20 panel PDFs) + battery comparison xlsx to be folded in once G moves them into this folder — those give REAL UK quotes to tighten these public averages.

solar_pv.unit: GBP per kW installed, MCS-certified, incl panels+inverter+scaffold+install
solar_pv.panels: Modern panels 400-450W each. ~9-10 panels per 4kW, ~13-15 per 6kW.

quote_check_flags.notes: Above ~£1,800/kW = high, push back or get another quote. Below ~£1,150/kW = check panel/inverter brand, MCS status, warranty, and whether scaffolding is really included. Economies of scale: £/kW should FALL as system grows, so a big system priced like a small one is a red flag.

battery_storage.unit: GBP per usable kWh installed (hardware + labour)
battery_storage.install_uplift: Standalone install adds £500-£1,500 depending on property/electrics.

quote_check_flags.notes: Modular installer-led systems sit at the low end; all-in-one premium units (e.g. Tesla, GivEnergy AIO) at the top. Above ~£1,000/kWh = premium — justified only by brand/warranty/integrated inverter. Compare like-for-like on USABLE kWh, not nameplate.

heat_pump_ashp.unit: GBP total installed for an air-source heat pump system (unit + cylinder + rads + labour)

ofgem_bus_average.basis: avg 8kW unit, Ofgem BUS stats Jan 2026

quote_check_flags.notes: ALWAYS check the quote is a proper MCS install with a room-by-room heat-loss survey (MCS requires one) — a heat pump sized off a rule-of-thumb is the biggest red flag and the main cause of poor performance. Confirm the £7,500 BUS grant is deducted at source by the installer, not something the homeowner claims back. Watch for undersized cylinders and skipped radiator upgrades that hide behind a low headline price.

ev_charger.unit: GBP for a 7kW home charger fully installed

grant.eligibility: renters, flat owners, on-street with cross-pavement solution, landlords — NOT standard owner-occupier with driveway

quote_check_flags.notes: Above ~£1,500 (outside London/SE) = high unless a long cable run or consumer-unit upgrade is genuinely needed. Ask what's driving any premium: cable distance, earthing/PEN protection, load management, groundworks.
